title: Investigator Workbench — flow insights & playback brainstorm
content:
Purpose
Quick brainstorming doc for an "Investigator Workbench"—a single-pane UX that helps engineers follow a performance incident start-to-end across related traces, spans and service boundaries. Focus is on interaction sketches, lightweight wireframe notes, and a prioritized backlog for grooming.

Goals
- Enable fast hypothesis generation: surface correlated traces and probable root spans without clicking into 20 traces.
- Preserve timeline fidelity: allow time-scrubbed playback of requests across services.
- Make filters composable and persistent across sessions and shareable with links.

Problem statement (observed pain)
- Oncall toggles between the trace list, trace details, logs and metrics tabs to correlate events. Too many context switches.
- Waterfall views across different traces have awkward alignment (timestamps drift) which makes cross-trace reasoning painful.
- Filters reset when you open a trace; no quick way to keep the same filter set while drilling down.

High-level idea
- Investigator Workbench: top-level timeline (global time ruler) + stack of lane rows (one lane per service/host/route). Each lane aggregates spans from many traces, aligned to the global time ruler.
- Selecting a suspect span highlights related spans in other lanes (same trace id correlation + causal heuristics).
- Time-travel playback slider: scrub to see how spans activate over time; supports play/pause and step-forward by span boundary.
- Focus mode: pin a span and collapse all non-related lanes into summarized rows to reduce noise.

Wireframe notes (textual)
- Left rail: persistent filter builder (time window, trace id, service, route, error tags, latency buckets, custom tag expressions). Filters are additive chips; click a chip to toggle scope-in or scope-out.
- Main canvas: global time ruler on top with mini-sparkline of request rate + error rate. Under that, lanes. Each span is a horizontal bar colored by status (green/amber/red). Span thickness encodes CPU/compute cost (heuristic).
- Hovercard: on hover show short summary (operation, duration, latency percentile, first log snippet, parent id). Card has two quick actions: "open full trace" and "pin to canvas".
- Breadcrumb trail above canvas shows active filters + pinned spans, with a share icon to copy permalink.

Interactions and microcopy
- Click on a span: open right-side detail rail (not modal). Rail contains full trace waterfall for that trace plus logs and metrics tabs. Back button returns to workbench with filters intact.
- Keyboard shortcuts: "k"/"j" jump to previous/next suspect span; "f" toggle focus mode; "/" open filter quick search.
- Filter scoping: shift-click on a chip will apply filter globally (persist across traces and sessions). Single-click applies only to current canvas view.

Automation heuristics (ideas)
- Probable culprit ranking: combine span error flags, long tail duration (>= P95 for that operation), and repeated callers. Show a "confidence" badge on suspect spans.
- Auto-correlation: when user pins a span, compute correlated traces within ±500ms window and show heatmap of similar spans.

Accessibility
- Ensure color-blind palette and pattern fills for critical vs non-critical spans.
- All interactions keyboard accessible; hovercards have focus equivalents.

Backlog (initial groomable tickets)
1) RW-INV-101: Canvas time ruler + aligned multi-lane layout (MVP). Acceptance: lanes align on global epoch; spans from at least 3 services rendered; zoom/pan works. Priority: P0. Owner: Miguel.
2) RW-INV-102: Pin-to-canvas and collapse non-related lanes. Acceptance: pinned spans persist in URL and in session storage. Priority: P1. Owner: Rina.
3) RW-INV-103: Hovercard + quick actions. Acceptance: hovercard shows operation snippet and two quick actions; performance <30ms on hover population. Priority: P1. Owner: Ethan.
4) RW-INV-104: Time-travel playback controls and step-by-span. Acceptance: play/pause plus frame-stepping implemented; playback syncs with trace detail rail. Priority: P1. Owner: Aisha.
5) RW-INV-105: Composable filter builder with shift-click scope toggle. Acceptance: filters persist across opening trace details and are sharable. Priority: P2. Owner: product-console.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- How expensive is computing cross-trace correlation at query time for large time windows? Consider sampling heuristics or precomputed correlation indexes.
- Do we start with service lanes (coarse) or route-level lanes (detailed)? Service lanes are less noisy but can hide hotspots.
- UX for high-cardinality tag filters — use tokenized input + autosuggest.

Design alternatives considered
- Snapshot compare mode: capture two time-slices and show diff of lanes (not prioritized for MVP).
- Inline logs vs side-by-side rail: inline keeps context but pollutes canvas — prefer side rail for now.

Next steps
- Quick spike: Miguel + Rina to prototype aligned lanes and time ruler (2-day spike). Deliver Figma frames and a short demo in next UX sync.
- Engineering spike: Ethan to explore query cost for cross-trace correlation and propose precomputation strategy (Linear ticket created).
- Sync with SRE: collect real oncall transcripts to validate common investigative flows (drop-in during next pager rotation).

Notes to self (loose ideas)
- Consider color hue shifting by trace sample id to visually group spans that belong to same trace even when distant in time.
- Add "suspect stack" microview: vertical list of top-5 suspect spans with one-click jump.

Referenced threads/links:
- Slack: #prod-observability thread 'johnny-prod-db-surge' 2025-01-28
- Linear: INF-927 (correlation pipeline exploration)

End.
